questions.prompt: You've told the agent three times not to create a worktree without committing first. It keeps forgetting. You want the rule to hold whether or not the model is paying attention. What should you build?
options: A PreToolUse hook on the worktree-creating tool, exiting 2 when the tree is dirty
Another section in CLAUDE.md, placed above the file rules so it gets read first
A skill that documents the rule, invoked at the top of each session
A subagent that reviews worktree creation after the fact and reports back
questions.explanation: A rule in the window is a request — it competes with everything else for attention and it compacts away. A PreToolUse hook runs outside the window, in your code, before the action, so it holds or it doesn't; there is no version of this where the model is 'forgetting' a hook. Option B is a stronger version of the thing that already failed three times. Option C is still a request, just packaged, and skills fire by judgment. Option D is strictly worse than the rule it replaces: it's a request plus a delay plus a report after the damage.

questions.prompt: A teammate asks why your project hook didn't replace the one in their user settings. Which answer is correct?
options: Settings files merge — both hooks run, so removing your project's copy leaves theirs live
The project file wins because it's closer to the working directory
Only the highest-precedence file that matches is loaded, and the rest are ignored
The user file wins, because user settings outrank project settings for security
questions.explanation: Hooks from every settings level merge rather than shadowing each other — that's why 'I removed the block' can leave a hook running from a file you forgot about. Option B inverts precedence: settings resolve toward user and managed levels, not toward the closest path. Option C describes override semantics, which is exactly what hooks don't do; a deny from one handler and an allow from another resolve by the deny > defer > ask > allow order, not by file. Option D sounds plausible for a security setting but isn't how hooks merge.

questions.prompt: You want a hook to tell the model that a file it just edited is generated build output, so it fixes the source next time. Which event and mechanism fit?
options: PostToolUse with additionalContext in a JSON object on stdout
PreToolUse with a deny decision, since the edit should never have happened
PostToolUse with exit 2, which undoes the edit and blocks the turn
SessionStart with a systemMessage listing the generated files
questions.explanation: additionalContext is exactly this: it goes into the model's context beside the tool result, so the model learns the fact it couldn't derive. It has to be PostToolUse because that's where the tool result is — and PostToolUse cannot block, so the 'deny' framing is unavailable. Option B puts the check before the edit, which would have to guess from the file path alone, and denies a legitimate write. Option C is the trap: exit 2 on PostToolUse does not undo anything — the file is already written — it only hands stderr to the model. Option D fires once per session, long before the relevant turn.
